core_obligations: Reduce to injective F (proof lines 9651-9654): the statement is immediate for F = 0 and is inherited from the graded pieces of a filtration by F-stable subspaces, so one may assume the kernel of F is zero.

Set up the matrix equation (proof lines 9657-9675): in a basis v_1, ..., v_n with F(v_i) = sum a_{ij} v_j, vanishing of the kernel forces the matrix (a_{ij}) to be invertible; multiplying by its inverse (b_{ij}) shows that solving (F - 1)(sum lambda_i v_i) = w is equivalent to the system lambda_j^p minus sum b_{ij} lambda_i = sum b_{ij} mu_i for j = 1, ..., n.

Build the auxiliary algebra (proof lines 9676-9685): let A be the quotient of k[x_1, ..., x_n] by the ideal generated by those equations; A is standard smooth over k because (b_{ij}) is invertible and the partial derivatives of x_j^p vanish, and the monomials with exponents less than p form a k-basis, so the k-dimension of A is p^n.

Conclude (proof lines 9686-9688): since k is algebraically closed, Spec(A) has exactly p^n points, which means that the fibre of F - 1 over each w has p^n points; in particular F - 1 is surjective and its kernel is a finite dimensional F_p-vector space of dimension at most dim_k(V).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the case of injective F by filtrations and the case F = 0.
Write F in a basis and invert the resulting matrix to turn surjectivity into a system of p-power equations.
Show the algebra defined by that system is standard smooth of dimension p^n over k.
Count its points using algebraic closedness of k to obtain p^n preimages for every w.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a frobenius linear endomorphism F of a finite dimensional vector space over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p has F - 1 surjective, with kernel of dimension at most dim_k(V) over F_p (statement lines 9640-9648). The proof combines three arguments: a reduction to the case of injective F via F-stable filtrations and the case F = 0 (proof lines 9651-9654), the inversion of the matrix of F to turn surjectivity into the system of p-power equations lambda_j^p minus sum b_{ij}lambda_i = sum b_{ij}mu_i (proof lines 9657-9675), and the construction of the algebra A defined by those equations, which is standard smooth because the partial derivatives of the x_j^p vanish and whose monomial basis shows dim_k(A) = p^n (proof lines 9676-9685). Surjectivity then follows by counting the p^n points of Spec(A) through algebraic closedness of k (proof lines 9686-9688). The claim is H2: three explicit steps, each short, with the algebra construction as the non-formal core.
